interest: Shows 1949 Japan phasing out special foreign-national food rations as supply stabilized, amid a 270-yen rate before the Dodge Line.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
United States Political Adviser for Japan
overview: This file (decimal file 894.5017) contains State Department correspondence from March and April 1949 concerning economic statistics, living costs, currency exchange rates, and food rationing in occupied Japan. It comprises two main exchanges: first, Despatch No. 189 from U.S. Political Adviser William J. Sebald in Tokyo (accompanied by a State Department Central Records replacement copy sheet and SCAP Diplomatic Section Note to the Australian Mission) notifying the Secretary of State that the Japanese Government would cease providing supplementary food rations to foreign residents on May 1, 1949, as basic ration levels had improved to 1,500–1,600 calories per day; and second, an inquiry from the International Committee of the YMCA regarding 1937 versus 1949 Japanese living costs and dollar exchange rates for American civilians, along with the State Department's reply referring the YMCA to SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section and citing the official exchange rate of 270 yen to the dollar.

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1947 and a diplomatic note concerning the termination of supplementary food rations provided by the Japanese Government to foreign nationals residing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports SCAP ending special food rations for foreigners in Japan after May 1949, as the Japanese ration reached 1,500-1,600 calories.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 189 on Supplementary Food Rations for Foreign Nationals in Japan (with Record Copy Replacement Form)

subfiles.about: Informs the Australian Mission that the Japanese Government will no longer provide supplementary food rations to foreign nationals residing in Japan after May 1, 1949.
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP tells Australia's mission foreign rations end after May 1949, since Japan's standard ration and markets now suffice.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Section Note to Australian Mission on Supplementary Food Rations for Foreign Nationals in Japan (Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 189)

subfiles.about: Answers a YMCA inquiry regarding living costs in Japan and states the official currency exchange rate of 270 yen to the dollar.
subfiles.summary: Bishop tells the YMCA State lacks Japan cost-of-living data, directing it to SCAP, and cites a 270-yen exchange rate.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State (Bishop) to International Committee of YMCA on Cost of Living and Exchange Rate
subfiles.to: International Committee of Young Men's Christian Associations

subfiles.about: Requests data on the current cost of living in Japan compared to 1937 and asks for the dollar exchange rate available to American civilians.
subfiles.summary: The YMCA asks State for 1949 versus 1937 Japan cost-of-living data and the current dollar exchange rate.
subfiles.title: Letter from International Committee of YMCA (Terrill) to Department of State Requesting Cost of Living and Exchange Rate Information
subfiles.to: Department of State (Far Eastern Division, Japan Desk)
